Do all your rough work in the booklet, using the blank spaces in the question booklet.

questions.enonce_markdown: The branch of production concerned with changing the location of goods is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Production has several branches. Extractive production takes raw materials from nature, manufacturing changes their form, and construction builds structures. **Commerce** is the branch of production that moves goods from the producer to the consumer, so it changes the place (and time) at which the goods are available, with the help of trade and its aids such as transport, warehousing, banking and insurance.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A trader bought goods worth 15,000.000 Frs. VAT is 19.25%. What is the amount payable?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The printed value "15,000.000 Frs" is read as 15,000,000 Frs. VAT is added to the price of the goods:

$$
\text{VAT} = 15\,000\,000 \times \frac{19.25}{100} = 2\,887\,500 \text{ Frs}
$$

$$
\text{Amount payable} = 15\,000\,000 + 2\,887\,500 = 17\,887\,500 \text{ Frs}
$$

Option A is only the VAT, and option C wrongly subtracts it from the price.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which insurance principle must an insured follow when filling the proposal form?
questions.corrige_markdown:
The proposal form is the document in which the person who wants cover gives the insurer the facts about the risk. The principle of **utmost good faith** (uberrima fides) requires the insured to disclose every material fact honestly; concealing or falsifying a fact makes the contract voidable. Contribution applies when several policies cover the same risk, insurable interest is the financial stake in the thing insured, and proximate cause is the main cause of a loss when a claim is settled.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Shop lifting is common to all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Shoplifting (theft of goods by customers who pretend to shop) can only happen where customers walk in and handle the goods themselves: mobile shops, department stores and hypermarkets. In a **mail order business** the customer orders from a catalogue and the goods are sent by post or carrier, so customers never enter a shop and shoplifting does not occur.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following services are performed by wholesalers to retailers EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Steady flow of goods.   B) Warehousing.   C) Information.   D) Variety of goods.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A wholesaler buys in bulk from producers and sells in smaller quantities to retailers. Services to retailers include ensuring a steady supply of goods, offering a variety of goods from many producers, giving information on new products, prices and market trends, and often credit and delivery. **Warehousing** (storing large stocks) is the service that the wholesaler gives mainly to the producer, who is relieved of the cost of storage; it is therefore the option that is not a service to retailers.

**Intended answer: B (Warehousing).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: A commercial bank will NOT need the information below before granting a loan:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Before granting a loan the bank needs to know how much is borrowed, for how long (duration), how the borrower will repay (method of repayment) and what security (collateral) is offered in case of default. The **name of the bank** is the lender's own name, which the bank already knows, so it is not information it needs from the borrower.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The mode of transport that is a feeder to other transport systems is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A feeder carries goods and passengers between the places of production or consumption and the main routes of other systems. **Road transport** is flexible and offers door-to-door service, so lorries and vans bring goods to railway stations, ports and airports and distribute them again on arrival. Canal, rail and sea transport run only between fixed terminals.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are agents in the London Freight market EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The freight market (the Baltic Exchange in London) brings together shipowners and merchants who need cargo space. Its agents are shipbrokers, chartering agents and independent brokers, who arrange charter parties and freight rates. A **del credere agent** is a commission agent in the sale of goods who, for an extra commission, guarantees that the buyer will pay. This is not a function in the freight market.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Duties which are imposed on imports based on the unit of measurement are known as:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **specific duty** is a fixed sum charged per unit of measurement of the imported good (for example per kilogram, per litre or per item), whatever the value of the good. An ad valorem duty is a percentage of the value. Customs duty is the general name of taxes on imports, VAT is a tax on value added, and excise duty is charged on certain goods produced at home.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The formula: $\dfrac{\text{Index of Export Prices}}{\text{Index of Import Prices}} \times \dfrac{100}{1}$ means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The ratio of the index of export prices to the index of import prices, multiplied by 100, is the **terms of trade**. It shows how many imports a country can obtain for a given quantity of exports: a value above 100 means that export prices have risen faster than import prices (a favourable change). It is not an exchange rate, which is the price of one currency in another.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following documents is issued to confirm payments of goods?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **cash receipt** is given by the seller to the buyer as proof that payment has been received. An invoice is a request for payment listing the goods and prices, a pro forma invoice is a preliminary quotation sent before the sale, and a consignment note accompanies goods being carried.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The day to day running of a joint stock company is in the hands of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a joint stock company the shareholders own the business but do not manage it. They meet in the General Assembly (annual general meeting) to elect the directors and take major decisions. The **Board of Directors**, elected by the shareholders, is responsible for the running of the company and appoints the managers who carry out the daily work. The General Assembly meets only occasionally.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The following investors enjoy limited liabilities EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Limited partners (in a limited partnership), equity holders and shareholders risk only the amount they invested. The **active (general) partner** takes part in the management and is personally liable without limit for all the debts of the business, so he is the one who does not enjoy limited liability.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Quality control is the main role of which of the following departments?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Quality control means checking that goods meet the required standard while and after they are made. It is carried out in the **production department**. Marketing studies the market and promotes goods, and the sales department sells them. There is no separate department simply called "Control" in the usual organisation of a firm.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The category of wants satisfied by services is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Wants satisfied by goods are material wants because the goods can be touched. Services such as teaching, banking, transport or medical care cannot be touched or stored, so the wants they satisfy are **immaterial** wants.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The difference between visible exports and visible imports during a trading period is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Visible items are physical goods. The value of visible exports minus the value of visible imports over a period is the **balance of trade**. The balance of payments is wider: it also includes invisibles (services) and capital movements. Terms of trade is a ratio of price indices.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Enterprises would NOT be classified using:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Enterprises are classified by size, which is measured by the number of employees, the capital invested or the turnover. "Longitivity" (meaning how long the business has existed, that is longevity) is not a criterion of classification.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Public Limited company starts operating when a:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A public limited company goes through two stages. The certificate of incorporation gives it legal existence, but it cannot yet start business or invite the public to buy shares. After the minimum capital has been subscribed it receives a **certificate of trading** (trading certificate), which allows it to begin operating. The prospectus and the articles of association are documents used during formation.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used to correct errors of undercharge in an invoice is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When the seller has charged too little on an invoice, he sends the buyer a **debit note** for the extra amount, which increases the debt. When the seller has charged too much (overcharge) or goods are returned, he sends a credit note, which reduces the debt.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The term '30 days net' means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
"30 days net" is a credit term: the full invoice amount (net, without cash discount) must be paid within 30 days of the invoice date. No cash discount is offered under this term.

**Answer: A.**

choix.texte: Payments of goods is due in 30 days time.
Discount is offered up to the 30th day.
After 30 days no cash discount is allowed.
Cash discount is allowed on the 30th day,

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these modes of transport is best suited for the transportation of perishable goods over long distances?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Perishable goods such as fresh fruit, flowers or fish spoil quickly, so speed is the main requirement over a long distance. **Air transport** is the fastest mode and therefore the best suited, in spite of its high cost. Rail, road and water are slower over long distances.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of days set aside for loading and offloading of ships is called?
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a charter party, the days agreed for loading and unloading the ship are called lay days. None of the options is worded exactly "lay days", but "lay day charge" is the only one that refers to them. Demurrage is the compensation paid to the shipowner when the lay days are exceeded, dead freight is payment for space booked but not used, and freight rate is the price of carriage.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Direct debit is suitable for:

*Options as printed:* A) Regular payments at regular intervals.   B) Regular payments at irregular intervals.   C) Irregular payments at irregular intervals.   D) Irregular payments at regular intervals.
questions.corrige_markdown:
A direct debit is an instruction by which the payer allows a creditor (for example a utility company) to collect money from his account whenever the amount is due. Because the creditor starts the payment, the **amounts and the dates may vary**, unlike a standing order, which pays a fixed amount at fixed regular intervals (option A). Among the printed options the best match is irregular payments at irregular intervals.

**Intended answer: C (Irregular payments at irregular intervals).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The payee in a bill of exchange transaction is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A bill of exchange is written by the **drawer** (the creditor, who sells the goods) ordering the drawee (the debtor) to pay a sum on a fixed date. The drawee who signs to accept becomes the acceptor. The payee is the person to whom the money is paid, which is normally the drawer himself. The drawee pays, so he is not the payee, and the domicile is the place of payment.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these forms of advertising does not target a particular audience?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Direct advertising (letters, leaflets and messages sent to chosen people) is aimed at a particular audience. **Indirect advertising** uses mass media such as radio, television, newspapers and billboards, which reach everybody and are not aimed at specific people. Persuasive and informative advertising describe the purpose of an advertisement, not its audience.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The main aim of personal selling is that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In personal selling a salesperson talks to the customer face to face. The main advantage is **immediate feedback**: the seller sees the customer's reaction, answers questions and objections, and adjusts the message at once. It is costly and slow in covering a large market, and it does not guarantee a quick rise in sales.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: There is immediate increase in sales.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following are the roles of advertising EXCEPT:

*Options as printed:* A) Introduce new products.   B) Persuade customers to buy.   C) Create additional demand.   D) Build image of the firm.
questions.corrige_markdown:
Advertising informs customers about products, persuades them to buy, creates additional demand and builds the image of the firm. Of the options, "introduce new products" is the least a role of advertising itself: the firm introduces a new product by developing and launching it, and advertising only makes it known.

**Intended answer: A (Introduce new products).**

The printed question is not reliable enough to be marked automatically so it is left open for self-assessment instead of being auto-marked.

questions.enonce_markdown: The term 'legal entity' implies:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A legal entity (artificial or juristic person) is an organisation, such as a company, that the law treats as a person separate from its owners. It can own property, make contracts and **sue and be sued** in its own name. A natural person is a human being.

**Answer: B.**

choix.texte: Can sue and cannot be sued.

questions.enonce_markdown: The document used to inform buyers of goods on transit is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The seller sends the buyer an **advice note** to announce that the goods have been despatched and will arrive soon, giving details of the goods and the means of transport. A consignment note is the transport document that goes with the goods, and a delivery note is signed by the buyer when the goods arrive.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of the following is NOT a function of the warehouse?
questions.corrige_markdown:
A warehouse stores goods, reduces the risk of loss, damage or theft, and stabilizes prices by releasing goods when supply is short and holding them when supply is plentiful. Making a profit is the objective of the business that owns the warehouse, not a function of the warehouse itself.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Which of these ocean vessels has a flexible schedule?
questions.corrige_markdown:
Liners (cargo liners and passenger liners) sail on fixed routes at fixed times. **Tramp ships** have no regular route or timetable: they go wherever cargo is available and are hired under a charter party, so their schedule is flexible.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Commercial banks perform the following functions EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Commercial banks accept deposits, lend money (loans and overdrafts) and keep valuables safely. Regulating the supply of money in the economy is the task of the central bank (in Cameroon, the BEAC for the CEMAC zone), not of commercial banks.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Regulate supply of money to the public.

questions.enonce_markdown: The following are government departments that protect consumers EXCEPT:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The departments of commerce, public health and housing and town planning are parts of government and enforce rules on prices, quality, health and safety. A **Consumers' Association** is a private, voluntary group of citizens, not a government department.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Department of housing and town planning.

questions.enonce_markdown: The document that serves as a temporal evidence of an insurance contract is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **cover note** is a temporary document issued by the insurer to show that cover is already in force while the policy is being prepared. The policy is the permanent and full proof of the contract.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: An example of an uninsurable risk is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A risk is insurable if there is an insurable interest and the loss can be measured and happens by chance. Fire, burglary and (in many policies) natural disasters can be insured. **Gambling** is a speculative risk, where one voluntarily bets to win or lose, so insurers do not cover it.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A balance of payments deficit implies that:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The balance of payments records all payments and receipts between a country and the rest of the world. A deficit means that **payments abroad exceed receipts**. Option B describes a deficit in the balance of trade, which covers visible goods only.

**Answer: C.**

choix.texte: Payments abroad are more than receipts.
Receipts are more than payments abroad.

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that visible exports are 2,500,000 Frs. and visible imports are 4,000,000 Frs. the balance of trade is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$
\text{Balance of trade} = 2\,500\,000 - 4\,000\,000 = -1\,500\,000 \text{ Frs}
$$

The balance is a deficit of 1,500,000 Frs, because imports are larger than exports. The printed option C gives the amount of the deficit. Option B is the sum of exports and imports, which is not the balance.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Business losses in a limited liability company are borne by:
questions.corrige_markdown:
The shareholders own the company and carry its losses, but only up to the amount they invested in shares. Debenture holders are creditors who must be paid their interest and capital, and directors are only managers.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Visible imports means:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Visible imports are physical **goods bought from abroad**. Goods sold abroad are visible exports, and services bought or sold abroad are invisible items. Option C, "buying goods from abroad", describes the action rather than the goods, so the best match is D.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The purchase of goods using coins in the absence of the retailer is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **auto vending** a machine (vending machine) delivers drinks, snacks and similar items when the customer inserts coins, so no shop assistant is present. Self-service means that the customer picks goods from shelves and pays at a till.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A document used to instruct banks to make regular payments at regular intervals is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
A **standing order** is a written instruction to the bank to pay a fixed amount to a named person at regular intervals (rent, insurance, loan repayment) until cancelled. The form on which the customer gives this instruction is the standing order form.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A joint effort by firms to advertise a particular product is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **generic (collective) advertising**, firms of the same industry share the cost of promoting the product itself (for example milk, rice or cocoa) and not one brand. Competitive advertising pushes one firm's brand against others.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The difference between turnover and cost of goods sold is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
$$
\text{Gross profit} = \text{Turnover (sales)} - \text{Cost of goods sold}
$$

For example, with sales of 500,000 Frs and a cost of goods sold of 350,000 Frs the gross profit is 150,000 Frs. Net profit is obtained after deducting the other expenses from gross profit. Margin and mark-up are percentages of the sales or of the cost.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A payment method used by bank customers to settle several bills with a single cheque is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In a **credit transfer** (bank giro) the customer writes one cheque, with a list of the creditors, and the bank transfers the right amount to each creditor's account. A bank draft is a cheque drawn by the bank, a standing order pays one creditor regularly, and direct debiting is started by the creditor.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The transfer of money into and out of an enterprise is termed:
questions.corrige_markdown:
Money moves into the enterprise (inflow of funds, such as sales receipts) and out of it (outflow, such as payment of expenses). Together, the movement of money in both directions is called the **financial flow**. Inflow and outflow each describe only one direction.

**Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Commerce developed as a result of:
questions.corrige_markdown:
When people and regions began to **specialize** in the goods they produce best, nobody produced everything they needed. Exchange of goods became necessary, and commerce (trade and its aids) developed to bring them from producers to consumers.

**Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A mail service in which minimal compensation is made for missing items is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
In **recorded delivery** the post office keeps a record of posting and delivery and obtains a signature, but pays only a small fixed compensation if the item is lost. Registered post is more secure and pays compensation up to the declared value, and express delivery is simply faster.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The full meaning of ATM is:
questions.corrige_markdown:
ATM stands for **Automated Teller Machine**, a machine with which bank customers can withdraw cash, check their balance and carry out other operations without a bank clerk.

**Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A cheque drawn today with a future date of payments is known as;
questions.corrige_markdown:
A cheque carrying a date later than the day on which it is written is a **post-dated cheque**; the bank will not pay it before the date written. A stale cheque is one presented more than the normal validity period (usually six months) after its date.

**Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: A department that provides information used by management to make decisions is;
questions.corrige_markdown:
The **accounting department** records transactions and prepares financial statements, costs and budgets, which management uses to decide on prices, investment and control. The production department makes goods, the human resource department manages staff, and the research and development department designs new products.

**Answer: B.**
